label: sequence began with digit 2: original steps t>=3 through <DEL>
explanation: Fires when the first original token was the digit 2. It is active on every original-phase step from t=3 onward and on the <DEL> step, so it acts as a long-range memory of first_tok==2 that persists until copying begins. It is silent at t=0-2 and essentially silent through the copy phase, including at the step that outputs the 2. Activation rises over t=3-5, peaking around t=4-5, then declines toward <DEL>. The very strongest examples start with 2 2, but such sequences carry only about 5% of the mass. Most missed activations are weak firings (<0.2 of max) in sequences where 2 is the second token rather than the first. Including those raises recall but drops precision to 0.58. The current input token has almost no effect on whether it fires.

issues: Small systematic false-positive class: when the sequence starts '2 x 2 ...' (orig(2)==2), the feature never fires at t=3. Score is 0/565 predicted steps on test, and these make up most of the 739 FPs. It turns on one step late instead: the same sequences at t=4 have precision 0.975. Excluding the class only moves test precision from 0.990 to 0.998 and F1 from 0.910 to 0.913, so it is a minor refinement.

The claim that the current input token has almost no effect is slightly overstated. When the previous input was a 2 (first_tok==2, prev_tok==2, t>=3), precision falls to 0.77. A recent repeat of 2 dampens the feature somewhat, but this affects only about 2% of the mass.

The low-activation quartile is only 38% covered. About 80% of the misses are weak firings in sequences where orig(1)==2 and first_tok!=2. On its own that class has precision 0.15 and holds 2.7% of the mass. The union predicate gives precision 0.576, recall 0.97 and F1 0.72, which matches the explanation's claim of 0.58. This is acknowledged weak spillover, not a hidden class.

The other claims hold on test. The copy phase is silent: first_tok==2 & phase==2 has precision 0.0005. t=0-2 is fully silent. The delimiter step fires with precision 0.99. Activation mass by t peaks at t=4-5 and declines afterwards.
